title: Contrast, target size and respecting reduced motion

videos.script:
A contrast ratio is not an opinion. {{math}} It is arithmetic: the light two colours give off, the lighter over the darker. Twenty-one to one is black on white. Text needs four and a half.

Today the planner gets a dark theme. {{dark}} A second palette, and every pair in it has to pass again. The first try keeps the old green, which reads on white and fails on black. Two tests find it from two sides.

Then three things people ask of a page. {{target}} A button big enough to hit: at least twenty-four pixels. {{motion}} No movement for somebody who asked their system for less. {{reflow}} And a page that works at three hundred and twenty pixels wide, which is what four hundred percent zoom leaves.

One fix breaks another, and the test from two sections back catches it. That is the point of running them all, every time.

And then the course ends where each part of it ended. A test checks what somebody thought to ask. The rest is still a person's job.
